title: Mandatory Selection Gate Matrix for Temporal Evidence Families

gates_definition.G1_Identifiability: Can the mechanism distinguish histories that B0 aliases? (B0(H_atk) == B0(H_ben) while Q(H_atk) != Q(H_ben))
gates_definition.G2_Non_Redundancy: Does it add temporal information absent from B0 without merely duplicating EWMA, sliding windows, or slow burn?
gates_definition.G3_O1_Implementation: Constant memory (scalar registers) and constant-time per-step updates (no packet history buffers).
gates_definition.G4_Benign_Measurability: Can its benign noise floor and stationary distribution be empirically characterized from the available chronological telemetry?
gates_definition.G5_Pacing_Robustness: Does it avoid trivial evasion under simple timing delays within the tested cyclic exploitation model?
gates_definition.G6_Interpretability: Does the state variable have a clear, auditable operational meaning suitable for a Zero-Trust architecture?

surviving_mechanisms.justification: Family C is the ONLY candidate that satisfies all six mandatory gates. It provides true identifiability on B0-aliased states, introduces a non-redundant proximity metric with a benign deadband, runs in O(1) time and space, possesses a clean empirical benign noise floor, resists pacing within the tested 1:10 exploit schedule, and conveys an intuitive Zero-Trust operational meaning (near-threshold probing exposure).
